clue.text: Type of insurance got by number crossing road per annum

indicators.note: the number spans or straddles the other pieces, holding them within it

parts.note: thirty is a number
PA is the abbreviation for per annum, yearly

explanation.surface: A puzzle about working out an insurance premium from a road number and an annual figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Third-party cover is the minimum kind of motor insurance, protecting other people rather than the policyholder's own car.

parts.note: T is the short form of time
to ape is to imitate or copy

explanation.surface: Someone has only a moment to duplicate a recording.
explanation.definitionFit: To tape something is to record it, on cassette or video.

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to set up or initiate something, such as an inquiry
as a noun, an educational or learned establishment, of which a college is one example

explanation.surface: Someone is about to begin at college.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning initiate and a noun for an organisation such as a college.

indicators.note: the drink is placed ahead of the single letter in the answer

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: A theatregoer has a quick drink before the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a work for the stage, a synonym of a play.

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the word before it are put out of order

explanation.surface: Garments make their appearance on a washing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal; 'line' looks like a washing line but is only the abbreviation L.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal word for clothing and garments.

clue.text: Sporting cry from friend wearing hot pants

indicators.note: the friend has the other letters on, so sits inside them
pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters of hot are made a mess of

parts.note: an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A friend in hot pants gives a cry at a sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is British slang for rubbish, here an anagram signal; 'wearing' puts the friend inside the jumbled letters (T..HO).
explanation.definitionFit: Tally-ho is the cry of the fox hunter on sighting the quarry, hunting being a field sport.

parts.note: a nub is a small lump or knob

explanation.surface: A jeweller trims a tiny gold nugget a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone, in the sense of ignoring them pointedly, is to snub them.

parts.note: NO is the column heading for not-outs in cricket batting averages
barking is British slang for crazy, mad

explanation.surface: A dog called Rover is indoors and barking.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter who ends an innings unbeaten is 'not out'; averages tables abbreviate these as NO.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover is a wanderer, and a nomad is one who wanders without a fixed home.

clue.text: A slave: Tiffany Case in 'Diamonds Are Forever', for example

definitions.text: Tiffany Case in 'Diamonds Are Forever', for example
definitions.meaning: Tiffany Case is the heroine of the 007 novel and film, read as the spy's woman

explanation.surface: A description of a Bond girl character, with a slavery angle.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman in bondage, a female slave; split differently it is the woman belonging to James Bond.

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a chiller is a frightening story

explanation.surface: A playwright has written a unique horror story.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Schiller was a German playwright, author of Mary Stuart and William Tell.

parts.note: something finished is over and past

explanation.surface: A diner has polished off a plate of tagliatelle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagliatelle is one example of Italian noodles, hence 'say'.

indicators.note: complex here means intricate or tangled, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A senior officer has a male constable inside a building complex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' is the indicator for rearranging MALE COP IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer is another name for a constable on the force.

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: around signals the wall hanging is turned backwards

parts.note: an arras is a tapestry wall hanging

explanation.surface: A detective loitering around Scotland Yard causes a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging' looks like loitering but is a tapestry; 'around' turns it backwards. 'Yard' suggests Scotland Yard but is just Y; 'causes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Disarray is a state of disorder and muddle.

clue.text: River's current beginning to deceive us

parts.note: something current is fashionable, in

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A river's current starts to trick the swimmers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like the river's flow, but means IN, as in fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is a great river of Pakistan.

clue.text: Familiar expert entertaining charmingly old-fashioned daughter

indicators.note: the expert hosts, so holds within it, the next piece

parts.note: an ace is an expert
quaint means attractively old-world

explanation.surface: A specialist welcomes a sweet, old-fashioned girl into the family.
explanation.definitionFit: To be familiar with something is to know it, to be acquainted with it.

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for the local body is said aloud

parts.note: a council runs local government

explanation.surface: A lawyer comes from the town council to give evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel is the term for a barrister or barristers acting in a case.

clue.text: Retire from stage suffering from depression?

parts.note: a step is a stage in a process
someone depressed is down

explanation.surface: An actor quits the theatre because of depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage' suggests the theatre, but it is a STEP.
explanation.definitionFit: To step down is to resign or withdraw from a post.

clue.text: One having left 'Lorna Doone' novel in a US city

indicators.note: having left says the letters of the first word are taken out of the title
novel means new, so the remaining letters are put in a new order

parts.note: a Victorian romance novel by R D Blackmore

explanation.surface: Someone has left behind a copy of the novel Lorna Doone in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing O, N, E from LORNA DOONE leaves LRNADO, which 'novel' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando is a city in Florida, home of big theme parks.

clue.text: Wistfulness of Saint Olga once abroad?

indicators.note: abroad means scattered or astray, so the saint's name is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: The longing felt by a saint called Olga when she was living overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a sentimental longing for the past or home.

definitions.meaning: having no effect, of no help
split in two, the word is the instruction to consume less

explanation.definitionFit: Something ineffectual is of no use; split, the word is the green plea to use less.

indicators.note: gruesome suggests a horrid mangling, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A class examines some horrible human remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a small class of students meeting to discuss a subject.

clue.text: Male teacher, halving a bill brought over, points to coffee-shop worker

indicators.note: the whole construction is turned over, read backwards
the male teacher splits the bill into two parts by going inside it

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as at a bar
pupils address a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster splits a bill with a colleague in a café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halving' puts SIR into A TAB to give ATSIRAB, and 'brought over' reverses it. 'points to' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A barista is someone who makes and serves coffee in a café.

clue.text: Large instrument could be graduate's in a short while

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate, with the possessive S
soon means before long

explanation.surface: A big musical instrument might soon belong to a graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: The bassoon is a large woodwind instrument of low pitch.

clue.text: Did nothing with papers left by editor

parts.note: ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: An editor left some papers and did no work.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to laze about doing nothing.

definitions.meaning: a vassal owing feudal service to a lord
a city in eastern Belgium on the Meuse

explanation.surface: A school topic about a Belgian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a feudal vassal and is also a city in Wallonia, Belgium.

clue.text: Academic unhappy about the newspaper's name appearing here?

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, an academic

indicators.note: the sad piece goes about, around, the following word

parts.note: sad means unhappy

explanation.surface: A miserable scholar complains about the paper's title.
explanation.definitionFit: The masthead is the title block at the top of a newspaper's front page.

indicators.note: headless means the first letter of the ghostly word is removed

parts.note: shades are ghosts or spirits

explanation.surface: Decapitated ghosts haunting the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Hades is the Greek underworld, the realm of the dead, used as a byword for hell.

clue.text: Also after leader of backing group

indicators.note: the word for also comes after the single letter in the answer
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A backing singer has also joined the group.
explanation.definitionFit: A band is a group of musicians.

clue.text: Trained at kendo fencing wife — old martial art

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so the rearranged letters surround the wife
trained suggests drilling into new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone trained in kendo and fencing alongside a wife in an ancient martial art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trained' is the anagram signal for AT KENDO, and 'fencing' means enclosing, not swordplay. 'old' gives only the final O, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Taekwondo is a Korean martial art of kicks and punches.

parts.note: to dog someone is to trail them closely
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A child shadows a parent's beliefs closely.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a set of principles laid down as authoritative, a doctrine.

definitions.meaning: a person's usual food and drink
a legislative assembly, as in Japan's or the historic ... of Worms

explanation.definitionFit: The word means one's habitual food and also a formal legislative assembly in some countries.

clue.text: Get up on piano and show off

indicators.note: in an across answer the standing piece comes on, after, the piano

parts.note: a grand is a grand piano
to stand is to get up

explanation.surface: A performer climbs onto the piano to play to the gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To grandstand is to behave ostentatiously to impress an audience.
